content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] community! I was asked by a friend to modify a program for his car wash using this smart relay. Since I hadn't worked with this device before, I installed the [product_name] demo software to test the logic. After finishing the program, I tried to figure out how to upload it to the device when I obtain the official software license. I selected "Tools" → "Select Hardware" → "Hardware type", but when I wanted to choose the [article_no] device from the dropdown, it was greyed out and an error appeared: "I7 input - block number too high". While researching the specs of this model ([article_no]) on the [company_name] site, I found it's an 8 input, 6 output relay – it was wired and programmed by another company originally. My question is: What should I do to get around this error? It seems I can't use any model below [article_no] standard.
I'm not sure why, but in my first post I could only upload a photo. Here's another attachment that might clarify the situation.

The device with order number [article_no] is a 12/24 RCE without display. In device selection, it's a [product_name] [version_no]. The key part of the order number is 08 -0BA0, meaning it's a [version_no] rather than an older [version_no].
With the demo software you can't upload programs to the device. You need to buy the paid software once, then you get free upgrades for a lifetime.
Thanks very much for the quick help. As soon as I'm at my laptop, I'll try to select the controllers you mentioned.
[user_name], I know uploading isn't possible, but I wanted to check compatibility with the mentioned controller before purchasing the license. Thanks for your time!

The latest software can be used with all previous hardware versions. You can import old programs into the new software. Just be sure to set the correct hardware version in your project's settings. You can't use new blocks or features with older hardware, but all the legacy blocks will still be available. Any type of connection to the unit is supported. Even hardware from 25 years ago can be programmed using the newest software. That's what's great about [product_name] software – buy it once and upgrade forever for free.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having difficulty matching device generations and article numbers to hardware types in the demo version of [product_name] software. Demo restrictions are causing confusion and unclear error messages when trying to select legacy hardware. Users value the full version’s broad compatibility with older and newer hardware, but the limited function and messaging of the demo version create early frustrations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to accurately select and test their hardware type and compatibility within the software before buying a license. They want clear messaging and to avoid mismatches and software errors that block their workflow.
